# The Shadow the Earth Casts

## Scripture
*"Why do you look at the speck of sawdust in your brother's eye and pay no attention to the plank in your own eye?… You hypocrite, first take the plank out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother's eye."* — Matthew 7:3, 5 (NIV)

## Reflection
On a clear November night, you can sometimes spot Earth's shadow: a dark, soft band rising in the east just after sunset, or sinking in the west before dawn. It's called the *belt of Venus*—a dusky blue-gray smudge that appears precisely *opposite* the sun. The shadow is always there. We simply need the right angle to notice it.

Here's the strange thing about this shadow: it's most visible when we stand *facing away from the light*.

Jesus knew something about shadows we'd rather ignore. When we fix our gaze on the faults of others—the speck in their eye—we've quietly turned our back on the Light. That's when our own shadow, the plank we've been carrying, rises into view. Not because we set out to be hypocrites, but because it's simply easier to name another's darkness than to let God illuminate our own.

Yet the belt of Venus holds a quiet promise. Earth's shadow is real, but it is *fading*—it dissolves into the coming dawn. So it is with us. When we turn back toward the Light, what we thought was permanent shadow proves to be only the place where grace hasn't reached *yet*.

Tonight, stand facing the sunset. Let the light show you what the dark has been hiding.

## Prayer
Lord Jesus, You are the Light that casts no shadow. Turn our faces from the faults of others and toward You, that we might see our own hearts honestly and let Your grace dissolve what we've carried too long. Amen.
